result.summary: DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 3 found three blocking lifecycle failures and one POSIX output regression.

findings.title: 1. BLOCKING: a starting broker can still be killed with its worker
findings.body: The worker is marked running before it creates a broker. Cancel reads broker presence once; if the broker spawns after that read but before the PowerShell tree snapshot, exclude is empty. The provisional record written after spawn is never re-read, so the kill can include the shared broker and its app-server subtree.
findings.recommendation: Serialize broker startup and worker kill across both the presence check and the destructive step.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING: a terminal job file can falsely prove cancellation
findings.body: Any non-running status sets workerFinished, including a failure written by the reaper. Direct app-server close can also return after five seconds with its child still alive. If the worker exits before an attempted kill, this flag makes cancel report success and overwrite the terminal record as cancelled, despite an unverified descendant tree.
findings.recommendation: Preserve an existing terminal result; do not report an unattempted Windows kill as cancelled without verified tree exit.

findings.title: 3. BLOCKING: failed broker startup drops an unverified ownership record
findings.body: When readiness times out, taskkill may fail and child.kill is only a best-effort fallback. The code then tears down files and clears the provisional broker record without confirming that the broker and its descendants exited. A live broker or app-server can become untracked.
findings.recommendation: Keep the ownership record unless the broker tree's exit is verified.

findings.title: 4. SHOULD-FIX: POSIX cancel output changes in a completion race
findings.body: The new workerFinished guard suppresses workerLeftRunning and its log line on POSIX when the worker finishes between selection and a refused kill. Main emitted that diagnostic in this case, contrary to the specified POSIX byte-identity boundary.
findings.recommendation: Apply the workerFinished suppression only on Windows.

next_steps: Fix the three blocking lifecycle paths, then exercise the startup and cancellation races on Windows.
Recheck POSIX cancel output against main and rerun the release CI matrix.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 3 found three blocking lifecycle failures and one POSIX output regression.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING: a starting broker can still be killed with its worker (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1346-1352)
  The worker is marked running before it creates a broker. Cancel reads broker presence once; if the broker spawns after that read but before the PowerShell tree snapshot, exclude is empty. The provisional record written after spawn is never re-read, so the kill can include the shared broker and its app-server subtree.
  Recommendation: Serialize broker startup and worker kill across both the presence check and the destructive step.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING: a terminal job file can falsely prove cancellation (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1356-1359)
  Any non-running status sets workerFinished, including a failure written by the reaper. Direct app-server close can also return after five seconds with its child still alive. If the worker exits before an attempted kill, this flag makes cancel report success and overwrite the terminal record as cancelled, despite an unverified descendant tree.
  Recommendation: Preserve an existing terminal result; do not report an unattempted Windows kill as cancelled without verified tree exit.
- [high] 3. BLOCKING: failed broker startup drops an unverified ownership record (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:302-317)
  When readiness times out, taskkill may fail and child.kill is only a best-effort fallback. The code then tears down files and clears the provisional broker record without confirming that the broker and its descendants exited. A live broker or app-server can become untracked.
  Recommendation: Keep the ownership record unless the broker tree's exit is verified.
- [medium] 4. SHOULD-FIX: POSIX cancel output changes in a completion race (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1365-1367)
  The new workerFinished guard suppresses workerLeftRunning and its log line on POSIX when the worker finishes between selection and a refused kill. Main emitted that diagnostic in this case, contrary to the specified POSIX byte-identity boundary.
  Recommendation: Apply the workerFinished suppression only on Windows.

Next steps:
- Fix the three blocking lifecycle paths, then exercise the startup and cancellation races on Windows.
- Recheck POSIX cancel output against main and rerun the release CI matrix.
